text:
Marathon Petroleum has lost nearly 19% over two weeks, with today's modest 1.2% decline continuing a sharp selloff that accelerated after the early November midterm elections. The core issue is geopolitical: recent news shows rising tension between the U.S. and Iran, despite Democratic gains in the midterms that typically favor renewable energy over oil refining. A potential conflict in the Middle East could disrupt global oil supplies and refining margins, which has spooked investors holding refiner stocks.

The timing matters here. Oil prices have actually stayed elevated (U.S. crude near $100/barrel), so this isn't a simple case of cheap oil hurting refiners. Instead, the political uncertainty—particularly the possibility of Iran conflict despite Democratic control of Congress—appears to be creating doubt about the sector's near-term stability, even though higher oil prices alone might normally support refining companies.
